input.question: Why are most orchestral pieces string dominated? And why are so many pieces written for that style of orchestra?
input.ground_truth: When brass instruments first came out they didn't have valves, so they could only hit a small variety of notes. This meant that all the melodies had to be carried by the strings, which were capable of hitting many more notes, and some like the Violin could even hit several octaves. There are some more recent pieces where the brass instruments are the ones carrying the melody, but I don't remember them off the top of my head.
